entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.0
entry.content:
# v3.7.0
## The version is just a number now
No more Beta, Stable or Unstable. Each of those made a promise about the build that the number already says better, and the last rename was itself a reaction to "Stable" claiming too much. A bare version claims nothing.
`Unstable-3.6.9` was the last of the old spelling; this is `v3.7.0`.
## Hunts now say where the target actually is
With the super-unique shuffle on, a hunt's target keeps its name but stands on some other boss's spawn point. Three separate displays were supposed to tell you that. None of them did, for three different reasons:
**The quest book showed nothing at all.** The code that looks up the moved target's real location sat behind a condition that could never be true — the line above it had already ruled out every hunt. It was dead from the day it was written.
**Zone names were off by one.** The area name table is indexed by area id directly, but the book read it one slot low, so every zone on the page named its neighbour. This is very likely why the hunt areas were written off as untrustworthy at the time: the table was right, the reading was wrong.
**The in-game tracker named the host but not the place.** It now says both.
A hunt reads `Found in: Black Marsh (at Rakanishu's spot)` when shuffled, and its own verified zone when not.
## Boss loot was invisible in solo runs
Every reward type announces itself so the launcher can log it and play a sound. Boss loot said "Awesome loot incoming!", which carried none of the markers the solo pipe filters on — so it produced no tracker entry and no sound, and always had. It now announces itself like everything else: `Drop: Andariel Loot (4 items)`.
Traps had the same problem and are fixed alongside.
## Debug menu
Unchanged from 3.6.9: `+100M XP`, `Max Level`, and `+10 Levels` giving ten actual levels.
Requires launcher 2.9.39.

## Randomized Start - Added Randomized Start - Has presets for niko, stations, towns and tos, but you can add any land entrance you like to the pool - Added free_starting_items option, cause most stations have no locations on an empty sphere 0. - start_with_train does a bit of railfinding, and will give you valid rails if your starting entrance leads to a train entrance.
## Entrance Randomization - Added entrance rando with the following groupings, that can either be shuffled by themselves or in 1 of 3 pools with other grouping. Dungeon options can also choose to only be shuffle with dungeon parts of the same dungeon: - shuffle_houses - shuffle_caves - shuffle_overworld_transitions - shuffle_stations - shuffle_train_transitions - shuffle_portals - shuffle_dungeon_entrances - shuffle_bosses - shuffle_dungeon_rooms - shuffle_blue_warps - shuffle_tos_staircase - shuffle_tos_entrances (not new, but has the new pool options) - shuffle_hyrule_castle - shuffle_disorientation (>:3) - shuffle_eote (ends of the earth) - shuffle_las (lost at sea) - Added the following entrance randomizer modifier options: - entrance_directionality: choose what pools and groupings care about pairing ups and downs etc. - decouple_entrances - ut_blocked_entrances: same as ph, choose how ut tracks blocked entrances. - Added entrance plando, with auto-pairing of orphaned entrances across groupings. - Adding option for changing the number of times ER tries to generate a valid layout, in case you want to play with volitile ER settings. - Added extended hint data when entrances are randomized
## Smaller new stuff - Added in-game warp to start! Same as ph, open the collection screen and flip to prime, then enter any transition or save and quit! - Added map warp! Tap a station on the map to prime a warp there. UT's `/get_logical_path` considers map warp when finding the shortest path. This can be disabled in host.yaml. - You remain in control during cutscenes for opening doors, extending bridges and hitting switches! - Added an option for non-progressive versions of bombs, bow and sword - Phantom Zelda now teleports to you whenever you try to enter a door without her - Added 3 missing big rupee locations in Dune Sanctuary - Added the /count_entrances client command, to check your entrance exploration progress. - Added an `all` option to plando_dungeon_pool - Opened the one-way passage from tunnel to the tower to the tower basement - Removed dungeons automatically open their boss doors, and give free small keys (in case ER wants you to pass through or something) - Locations sent from console now process in client, for things like sending ut events - Added open_blizzard_temple yaml option, the bell doors are always open - Added open_blue_warps yaml option, 2-way blue warps are always open - New UT events: - Unlocking blue warps - Unlocking train portals - Delivering NPCs that give rewards in other rooms to their stations. - Visiting Kagoron at the Mountain Altar - Finding the chest at Disorientation Station - Triggers in other ER rooms in marine temple - Unique rabbit locations when total rabbits are enabled - Stamp stations with vanilla stamps - Extra shortcuts - Added a yaml option to toggle extra UT events - UT's /get_logical_path can use unlocked shortcuts. - Many events will trigger backup activation of themselves if save data was lost after triggering them
## Bugfixes and tweaks - Fixed crashes from game trying to spawn demon trains on non-existant tracks. Forest glyph is now randomizable, as well as fire glyph without btt - Fixed gen bug where certain locations required a `player` amount of something - `both` option for dark realm access now cares about dungeons - Shattered compass mode no longer adds a completed compass to the pool - Boss key stuff should no longer crash! - Fraaz can now logically be killed with more than sword (most weapons hit through his big form's chargeup!) - Oops some events did not have data. - no_cargo now removes all lava in Goron Village - Ferrus now spawns in fire realm with ocean source - Hearts no longer get stolen at max health - Farmabe chests in LAS give treasure on repeat visits. final chest does not when rooms are shuffled - Quitting on the train no longer sends rabbit locations - Fixed catch 50 rabbits location - Fixed Linebeck treasure cave giving free rupees - Fixed Cactops giving free ocean source - Train parts are more consistent - Teao 3 unlocks without the previous levels if Teao 3 is a required dungeon - Fixed Teao 3 location - Stamps gotten with the vanilla stamp option persist through resets - Fixed item models for farmable chests on repeat visits - Client now actually fetches most server data on connecting rather than needing to wait until they get updated lol - Added a 10s timeout for precision operations - Saving and quitting was triggering events early, fixed it - Renamed starting entrance to Warp to Start - Prevented deathlink from processing during get item cutscenes - Fixed compass of light appearing in pool when playing with shattered compass - Failing to enter the dark realm sends goal requirement info - Added getting ToS 19f center chest without rotating repeaters with an off screen bow shot - Fixed model swaps for progressive item vanilla locations - Made progress on multi-version support - Sending extra progressive items sets the base item
Huge thanks to @catzador for doing tracker data entry and loads of playtesting before release!

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.1
entry.content:
# v3.7.1 — Crash & stability round (safe mid-run)
Every fix in this release is runtime-only: nothing changes the generated world, the check list, or item placement. It is safe to update in the middle of an ongoing multiworld — that is the whole point of it.
## Crash fixes
- **Fixed the "cow crash"** (assertion in UnitRoom.cpp / DungeonTestRoomGame). Every spawn the mod performs — Treasure Cow, cow hoard chests, trap ambushes, object traps — now resolves the room that actually CONTAINS the target coordinates before spawning. Previously the player's own room was passed with far-away coordinates, and the game asserts on that mismatch instead of failing gracefully; the cow's "30 placement attempts" never got a second try. The cow also spawns closer now (25-100 yards instead of 40-300), so its placement lands inside loaded terrain. - **Fixed the texture-cache crash** (glTextureCache.cpp / tTempItem). Object traps (barrels / urns / false treasure) only spawn object types that are already present in the area around you — an act-foreign object has no loaded graphics and killed the renderer. A trap that cannot fire safely fizzles silently instead of crashing.
## Traps
- **A "Trap: Monsters" filler no longer announces itself as the Monster Revive Trap.** The ambush queue now remembers who queued it: reward traps say "TRAP! Monsters incoming!", only the actual Revive Trap says "The slain rise against you!". (The Revive Trap toggle itself always worked — the message was lying.)
## Item delivery / progression
- **Raised both redelivery-protection caps** (applied-item ids 4096 → 16384, filler locations 2048 → 8192) and made hitting a cap log loudly. Anything that fell off these lists silently was re-delivered on the next reconnect — the "save & quit gave me 28 skill points" report. - **Settings now survive save & load correctly:** `xp_multiplier` was clamped by a leftover 1-10 guard on load (the setting goes 0-100 — an x25 player lost the multiplier every restart), and `skill_max_level` + `skill_level_reqs` were written to the state file but never read back.
## Gameplay
- **Treasure Cow rebalanced:** max 3 per act (was 5), 8% chance per area (was 25%), and early-act HP bonuses roughly halved. A boss-tier cow in Den of Evil at level 1 was not a fair fight. `treasure_cows.dat` overrides still apply if present. - **After a crash you can no longer keep a skill you don't own on left/right click** — the mod now validates hand-assigned skills continuously and resets unowned ones to Attack. - **One kill can no longer complete two Hunts.** A super-unique's minions share the boss's class, and the class-match fallback credited the minions' hunt on top of the boss's own — minions and champions are now excluded from fallback crediting. - **Clear Monastery Gate / Clear Inner Cloister** are now reach-the-area checks. Those zones spawn almost no monsters, so "kill 8" meant dragging monsters in from next door. Same treatment as the Tower Cellar fix in 3.0.0.
## Entrance shuffle
- **Exiting a cross-act shuffled dungeon returns you to the entrance you came from** instead of bouncing you town-to-town. The act-town lock used to wipe the recorded way home (this is what broke the Cain quest for one player), and zone-locking could override the return warp in the same tick. The original entrance always wins now.
## UI
- **The HUD tracker no longer draws on top of the open Book.**

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.2
entry.content:
# v3.7.2 — Settings, gold and a stuck-skill rescue (safe mid-run)
Game-side only. The launcher is unchanged (still 2.9.39), and so is every generated data file — **your monsters, bosses, entrances and vendors stay exactly where they are.** Safe to install in the middle of a run.
## Your settings actually apply now
- **Skill point cap was stuck at 20** no matter what your YAML said. The value arrived correctly from the server, then the character's own saved state overwrote it with a stale one. Under Archipelago the YAML is now the final word; standalone keeps its per-character settings as before. Same fix for "skill level requirements". No cleanup needed — it corrects itself on load.
## Gold
- **Gold rewards announced "0 Gold" while paying the real amount.** When gold became level-scaled the amount moved to where the character's level is known, but the message stayed behind and kept printing a hardcoded zero. You were always being paid; only the text lied. - *Experimental line only:* level-scaled gold was queued but **never actually granted** — four places added to the queue and nothing ever emptied it.
## Quality of life
- **Whirlwind (and any skill with its own animation) no longer traps you.** Start one holding a bow, crossbow or spear and the character used to freeze until you logged out. If you are stuck in a skill animation and haven't moved for three seconds, the game now nudges you free by itself. - **The "SOMETHING UNUSUAL IS NEARBY" warning** lost its black box — it was sized by guessing the pixel width from the character count, so it only ever covered the first half of the message. The text is also higher and further left. Both offsets are tunable in `d2arch.ini` under `[Notifications]` (`BigWarnOffsetX`, `BigWarnOffsetY`).
## Items
- **Quest items can no longer be handed out as random unique or set drops.** Six quest bases were reachable this way — the Viper Amulet, Khalim's Flail and Will, the Staff of Kings, the Horadric Staff and the Hellforge Hammer. Getting a spare could confuse or break the chain it belongs to. - **Every super-unique the mod adds has a real name.** All 45 showed up as "an evil force", which is also why a gate guardian standing next to its quest boss looked like a broken duplicate. They now read "Gatekeeper <name>", so you can tell the key-holder from the real thing.
## Not in this release
The monster, super-unique and shop shuffle rebalances are built and tested but deliberately held back: they change the generated world, and that would move things around mid-run. They ship once the current games are finished.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.3
entry.content:
# Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.3
## The Treasure Cow drops real loot now
Killing a Treasure Cow has paid out three different ways, and this is the one that should have been first: the game's own.
The cow is a superunique, and `SuperUniques.txt` gives every superunique its own `TC` / `TC(N)` / `TC(H)` treasure-class columns. The Cow King has always used his. The Treasure Cow's were empty, so it quietly fell through to the base monster's ordinary "Act 4 Unique B" — the same table any unique hell bovine gets. The cow was a boss that dropped like a regular monster, and everything built on top of that was compensation for it.
Those three cells now point at a new **AP Cow Hoard** table, one per difficulty:
- **10 picks, nothing wasted.** Diablo and Baal roll 7, and throw away 15% of them as no-drop. The cow rolls 10 and drops on every one. - **Better odds than any boss in the game.** Unique 400 / Set 550 / Rare 700, against Diablo's 983 across the board — lower is better here. Even the hardest vanilla superuniques only reach 512. - **Top-tier equipment.** It pulls from `Equip C`, the highest of the three equipment tiers. Baal pulls from `B`. - **Gems, runes, rings, amulets, jewels and all three charm sizes**, weighted so jewellery is not competing with gems for the same slot.
Because this is the engine's own drop path, **magic find applies** — properly, per item, the way it does on any other monster. So do quality rolls and item level. None of that was true of the previous payouts.
### What this replaces, and why
The first version handed items over through the mod's own item-creation call. That path knows nothing about magic find and gives up silently when the inventory is full, which is where every "the cow dropped nothing" report came from.
The second spawned sparkly chests and let the game fill them. The loot was real, but chests are solid objects: in a one-tile corridor one of them walls the player in, and a chest that cannot be placed anywhere is simply lost, so the reward shrank without saying so.
A treasure class has neither problem. Nothing is placed, so nothing can block a corridor and nothing can go missing.
## Under the hood
- The package no longer contains any Diablo II engine files. Everything shipped is either this mod's own code or open-source components; the game's own files come from your installation. See `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` for the full list of components, their authors and their licences. - New guard in the data-table gate: a blank line inside a `.txt` table is now a build failure. The game asserts on one (`Excel.cpp #646`) and the previous check could not see it, because it discarded empty rows before looking.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.4
entry.content:
# Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.4
## The vanishing waypoint menu, fixed at the source
The report has come in again and again: every act tab except Act 1 disappears from the waypoint menu — waypoints you have already activated stop showing up — and talking to one or two town NPCs, any of them, brings them all back at once.
That last detail was the clue. The waypoint bits themselves are never lost: the save is fine, and the game resends them every single time the menu opens. What goes stale is the client's copy of the *quest records*, which is what the menu uses to decide which act tabs to show. The client only learns those records when the server sends them — and in an unmodified game that happens constantly as a side effect of quest dialogue: the caravan NPCs and every quest-bearing conversation resend the full quest state. That is why "talk to Jerhyn" was the folk remedy, and why any other quest NPC works just as well.
This randomiser moves players between acts through its own gate system, so a whole session can pass without any of those resends ever firing. The menu was never being told what you had.
The engine keeps that resend in one small function of its own, and the mod now calls it on every area change and every ten seconds. The client's copy can no longer stay stale for longer than that — no NPC required. Like the mod's other engine calls, it verifies the function's first bytes before ever calling it, and disables itself cleanly if they do not match.
The launcher's KNOWN ISSUE note about this has been rewritten to match.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.5
entry.content:
# Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.5
A full playthrough's logs came in, and reading them found more than the report did. Four things here were never noticed by anyone playing — they were found by checking the game's own data against the code.
## You can no longer walk from Act 3 to Baal
The entrance shuffle moves dungeons around, and it assumes every dungeon it moves is a dead end: one way in, the same way out. Two Act 5 areas were in that pool and are not dead ends at all. **The Ancients' Way** opens onto Arreat Summit, and **Crystalline Passage** runs through to the open Act 5 tundra.
So a tester walked into a spider cave in Act 3, came out on the road to the Ancients, and finished the game from there. Both areas are now pinned in place, and a check that reads the game's own level connections refuses to build a release if a shuffled dungeon has a second way out. Removing the pin and running that check is how the fix was verified.
## Anya could end up behind the cow level
The cow level swaps places with a side dungeon chosen at random. Two were marked as safe to give up — and one of them was the Frozen River, where Anya is held prisoner. Roughly every other seed put a required quest behind Wirt's leg and a cube recipe. It never came up in the playthrough because that seed picked the other one.
The Frozen River is no longer a candidate.
## Eleven skills could break when they came from another class
Jab, given to a paladin holding a sword, was unusable and eventually crashed the game. The cause was a typo of sorts: Jab was listed as a throwing skill when it is actually a sequence skill, so the code meant to catch exactly this never looked at it.
Checking every class skill against those lists found **eleven** in the same state — Jab, Impale, Inferno, Lightning, Chain Lightning, Charge, Leap, Frenzy, Arctic Blast, Dragon Tail and Dragon Flight — plus four filed under a type they do not have, which is what made the lists look finished.
The lists are gone. The game now reads each skill's own animation type and decides from that, so no skill can be forgotten again.
## The Treasure Cow is at its intended difficulty
Version 3.6 toned the cows down to 3 per act at 8%, with health scaled as a percentage rather than a flat amount — flat health also multiplies a monster's regeneration, which is how they became unkillable in the first place. That change only touched the built-in defaults, and a configuration file shipping alongside it still carried the old numbers: **5 cows per act at 40%**, with flat health up to +100,000. The file won, in every install, for every player. The playthrough ran at 40% from start to finish.
## Fixes
- A crash-handler was quietly absorbing hundreds of faults per session — 356 in the playthrough, 338 of them from one function reading a game that had already been freed during loading. Its twin already guarded against this; this one did not. - Builds now produce a symbol map, so the next crash report can be read directly instead of being reconstructed by hand from register values. - Per-frame input and rendering traces are off unless switched on. They were 4,000 lines of a single session's log and buried everything useful.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.7.5r2
entry.content:
# Diablo II Archipelago 3.7.6
## The HD graphics, free resolution and 3D sound add-ons are no longer bundled
Three well-known community projects used to ship inside this package: **D2GL** (the Glide-to-OpenGL renderer that gives the game HD graphics and widescreen), **SGD2FreeRes** (which unlocks resolutions the original does not offer) and **DSOAL** (which restores the original 3D positional audio). They are gone from the download.
They are licensed GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0-or-later and LGPL-2.1. Those licences place conditions on *distributing* the software, and this project was not meeting them. The argument that they were separate programs merely travelling in the same folder is a real one — none of them is linked into this mod's code — but it is an argument, not a fact, and the cost of getting it wrong falls on the people who wrote them. So the question is no longer asked.
**Nothing is lost if you want them.** They are add-ons, not part of the mod, and the game runs without all three. The README now has a section explaining what each one does, linking to its author's own releases, and describing where the files go — the same way you already supply your own copy of Diablo II. Getting them yourself carries none of these obligations; it is only handing them out that does.
**If you already have them installed, nothing happens to them.** The update never touches files it did not install. Your existing D2GL keeps working exactly as before.
**If you install fresh**, the game starts on Diablo II's own DirectDraw renderer at the original resolution, until you drop D2GL in.
## The launcher tells you which add-ons it can see
Installing something by hand raises a question the launcher used to have no answer to: *did that work?* It does now, in three places.
**Settings → Diablo II Archipelago** has an **Optional add-ons** section listing all three with a status each — installed, not installed, or installed but inactive — plus what each one adds and a link to its author. A **Check again** button re-reads the folder, so you can alt-tab out, drop the files in, come back and click it without restarting the launcher.
**The game's Overview page** carries a small badge: `ADD-ONS: D2GL, DSOAL`, or `NO OPTIONAL ADD-ONS` when the folder is bare. It is deliberately grey and never counts against **READY TO PLAY** — these are optional, and the game is ready without them.
**The Play log** prints the same three lines every time you launch, right above the install check you already read.
One case gets called out specially. **SGD2FreeRes on its own does nothing** — nothing in this mod loads it; D2GL does, through `load_dlls_late` in `d2gl.ini`. Install it without D2GL and its files sit there doing nothing at all, which looks exactly like a broken download. The launcher now says *"Installed but inactive — nothing is loading it"* and tells you to install D2GL as well.
Detection is by the file that actually matters, not by the folder looking roughly right: `glide3x.dll` for D2GL — the very file `-3dfx` loads — and **both** `dsound.dll` and `dsoal-aldrv.dll` for DSOAL, so a half-finished copy reports as missing rather than as working.
The `START.bat` files print the same report before launching.
## The mod no longer assumes the resolution patch is there
`SGD2FreeResolution.json` is ours and always ships; SGD2FreeRes itself does not. The mod read that file to learn what resolution the game was running at — so without the component installed it laid out every panel, the quest book, the HUD tracker and the mouse mapping for 1068×600 while the engine was really drawing 800×600.
It now checks that D2GL and SGD2FreeRes are both actually present before believing the file, and falls back to the engine's real size otherwise.
The tuned settings this mod uses for those tools — `d2gl.ini`, `d2gl.json` and `SGD2FreeResolution.json` — are still included. Those are our configuration, not the tools, so the moment you install a component it is already set up the way this mod expects.
## Also
- `NOTICE` and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` now list only what the package actually contains, and say plainly which components were removed and why. - A release check reads the built ZIP and fails the release if any of those components reappears — including their licence texts, so the package carries the licence of exactly what is in it and nothing more. - The download is **12.3 MB**, down from 78.6 MB.

entry.title: Mega Man Zero 3 v0.3.0
entry.content:
A full rewrite! The world is now [built from a decompilation of the game](https://github.com/mmzret/rmz3) instead of patched into the ROM by hand.
Since this update is almost a total rewrite, so there could likely be a lot of undocumented bugs, so be sure to let me know in the Discord if anything seems off!
# New Features: - Item popups. You now get a little graphic on screen when another player sends you an item. - This is still a work in progress, as the icons currently don't actually represent what you've received. - There is now a disk counter on the pause menu, so you can see how many you're holding out of how many you need for your goal to complete. - The hub room lets you replay a stage you've already cleared, either as a free run or as the mission again. This lets you reattempt missions for another chance at an A+ rank clear, meaning that no checks in this world are missable. - The vanilla goal option has been removed. There used to be a "vanilla" option, where you just had to beat the final boss. It has been removed, and now the only goal is to beat the boss with the set number of secret disks given. If you want the old way back, you can just set required disks to 0. I didn't feel like maintaining both options, and I don't think many people used it anyway. # Bug Fixes - E-Crystals filler items should no longer be lost if you load earlier saves after being sent them. - Subtanks no longer delete their location check. Receiving a subtank from someone else used to despawn its pickup in the world, which made that location impossible to get. - Armor chips, subtanks, and crystals no longer get temporarily deleted by a game over, and now show up immediately when you load a save. - Fixed one of Sunken Library's disks not being reset when you load the level and have already been given the disk through an Archipelago item. - Removed the warning telling you not to save after the credits. New Game Plus works entirely now, and saving whenever should be fine too, but you should probably keep a save game on the last level just so you can revisit all levels in the game.

entry.title: Rogue Legacy 2 v0.1.0r2
entry.content:
Note: Please replace both the .apworld and the game mod files when updating to this version
### Improvements
- Add a colored tree which displays the upgrade paths in the manor. Manor locations are now named according to this tree (i.e. Manor - Red Path Upgrade 3) so that it is much clearer what a hint (or spoiler log) is referring to in the manor. - This can be toggled on/off using the Spin-Kick button - Added flavor text for foreign item descriptions which indicates whether it is progression, useful, or filler (or trap). - Manor items are no longer all marked as progression, only stat upgrades (assuming the YAML is configured to require some number of stat upgrades before biomes/bosses are considered "in-logic") are now progression. Things like class unlocks are not. This should provide a marginal improvement in success rate when generating worlds with stringent logic.
### New Config Options
1. reveal_manor_upgrades - (true/false, default: false), When enabled, all upgrades in the manor will be shown so purchases can be planned in advance. The normal purchase gating still applies; before you can purchase an upgrade, you must have purchased the previous upgrade in the manor. 2. trap_appearance - (hidden/visible, default: hidden), When 'hidden' traps are disguised as another item from the multi-world so that they can't be trivially avoided by looking at an item name before purchasing. After purchase, the trap's true name is revealed.
### Bugfixes
- Fixed a bug where in a specific scenario (all estuaries defeated and sun lantern received already) Johan would not spawn in Pishon Dry Lake to give the sun-lantern-conversation location check.
